mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (measured as the 3-month change) signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in FEDFUNDS decline periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained annualized inflation rate above 2.5% (as measured by CPIAUCSL) signals an impending monetary tightening and increased risk aversion, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in < 40% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising industrial production (INDPRO > 100) and falling housing starts (HOUST < 600) signals a resilient demand for goods and a cooling housing market, which together predict positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in < 40% of instances where INDPRO > 100 and HOUST < 600, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS rising above 0.1% in 3 months and CPIAUCSL above 2.5%), a rise in the federal funds rate predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in < 40% of triggered instances during monetary tightening cycles, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 5.0% signals economic distress and reduced corporate earnings potential, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in < 40% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising employment (PAYEMS > 130000) and falling unemployment (UNRATE < 10.0) signals a strengthening labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in < 40% of instances where PAYEMS > 130000 and UNRATE < 10.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 95) signals an economic slowdown that increases risk aversion and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in < 40% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (defined by HOUST > 600 and CPIAUCSL annualized inflation rate < 2.5%), a high housing market (HOUST) and moderate inflation signal overvaluation and potential for market correction, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 600 and CPIAUCSL annualized inflation rate < 2.5%
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in < 40% of triggered instances during late-cycle expansion, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
